- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., post-77.5+ peaks, model often overshoots to 78+).
- Underestimate downward corrections when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.10 to -0.30) — model tends to hold too high, fails to drop.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum (e.g., +0.50+ sentiment), model overreacts — cap forecast at +1.5% above recent high.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Lagged response: if sentiment turns negative after 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust — delay 1–2 days in downward correction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d high, reduce by 2–4% unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- For sentiment >0.05, model tends to overestimate — apply 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment unless price is already near 80+.
